notes: The page, numbered 36 in ink, gives a specialization of case a) as (91): two labeled vertices, a loop at the left vertex and a lower joining edge, with a visibly canceled upper arc. The written constraints are I1 amalg I2=I and g1+g2=g−1. The rational right-vertex condition is revised to on a card I2≥2 when g2=0. A live NB OPS margin proposes g2=1 and g1=g−2 provided g≥2, with an arbitrary partition (I1,I2) of I. These are manuscript statements; the existence and stability of the specialization are not proved here.

A limited exact algebra check verifies (g−2)+1=g−1 and, on adding one cycle, (g−2)+1+1=g. It also verifies (g-prime−1)+g-double-prime+1=g-prime+g-double-prime. These are only polynomial identities. Treating each live loop drawing as one loop plus one joining edge is the usual intended graph reading; the preserved pen gaps are not used to claim topological disconnection. The calculation does not establish a geometric specialization.

The manuscript gives case b-prime in (92), labeled by I-prime/I-double-prime and genera g-prime−1/g-double-prime. For g≥1 it says one may choose the notation so g-prime≠0, after exchanging the two genera, and obtain the common specialization b-prime=a-prime. It states that this proves the asserted result when g≠0. This global assertion and the needed hypotheses on the preceding cases are carried as manuscript claims; no other page was consulted and no proof of them is claimed.

For g=0, with inserted card I≥6, the manuscript says only the cases b) remain. A canceled attempt compares card I-prime with card I-double-prime and concludes card I-prime≥3, then it turns to the chain (93). The middle sketch is only partially canceled: the oblique path crosses b-double-prime, the wavy path crosses the two upper I labels, and the overworked lower glyph has its own cancellation. The lower two-point edge itself is not crossed and remains drawn. H’s editorial claim that the sketch is not struck does not override these separate visible states.

The final captions claim k segments, k+1 vertices and total marked weight 2+k on the left, with analogous ell counts on the right. Conditionally, a chain of n segments has n+1 vertices, and one weight 2 together with n weights 1 sums to 2+n. Exact coefficient arithmetic verifies that elementary identity. It supports the expected plus in a weight sum, but the written right-hand sign is predominantly horizontal and stays minus/plus doubtful. The missing upper weight at a_(k−1) is not supplied, so the arithmetic is not presented as a complete verification of every drawn weight.

The chain has ten explicit visible vertex marks. The one above written b_(-1) is open, the others are filled; no special geometric meaning is inferred from that visual difference. The b-index lacks a separate ell and is kept literally as b_(-1), with the expected b_(ell−1) sequence only noted here. The right ellipsis includes a continuing horizontal stroke and a lower wave. Local small gaps are reproduced. The right caption’s final I-double-prime area remains doubtful because it is overwritten.

The extra b-like glyph above live a-prime, the crossed preliminary g after éch., all fourteen textual cancellation units and the canceled upper arc are represented. All original doubtful canceled readings remain doubtful. The empty-set signs in the first canceled formula are long-stem phi forms. Punctuation is local: no semicolon after the marginal g≥2 condition, no terminal period after de I, and no trailing comma after inserted card I≥6 are supplied. H’s added autres, duplicate b-double-prime label and caption commas are not source ink; its prose descriptions and editorial notes are not copied into the transcription.

Forty-five physical writing bands were read. The count treats parallel labels/caption lines at a comparable height as one horizontal band: one ink header, the opening heading, four bands for the (91) graph labels including the overwritten upper glyph, five right-condition/revision bands, three marginal bands, a second heading and its canceled continuation, three (92) label bands, fourteen main-argument/revision bands, three middle-sketch label bands, eight final-chain/caption bands, and the pencil foliation. The whole scan and both native halves were viewed once; all eighteen saved crops were viewed. No OCR, internet search, other page, TeX compilation or blind second reading was used.

The separate lower-left pencil number is 73 and its hand attribution is uncertain. M1066 resolves only the live a-prime label. The new b-like glyph and its state remain doubtful independently. The comparison has fifty substantive rows; macro-only changes, the resolution of the a-prime doubt itself, and certainty-only additions such as the overwritten final I-double-prime doubt are not counted as additional text changes.
